claim_text: Explanations that surface the least-satisfied member raise perceived fairness relative to group-average framing; the underlying preference is for protecting the worst-off member.
Strategies that maximise one member's utility are perceived as less fair than balanced strategies.
Group outcomes with a higher floor of per-member satisfaction are rated more consensual than outcomes with the same mean but a lower floor.

source_paper: Quantitative Explanations on Fairness Perception in GRS (UMAP 2025)
claim_text: Reducing the spread of per-member satisfaction raises fairness perception even when the mean is unchanged.
